column4:
I prefer scenario 1 because it respects cultural diversity and allows different societies to develop appropriate AI systems based on their own values. In this way, each group can maintain its own identity rather than being assimilated by a single standard. Although it will bring compatibility issues, the "cultural translation layer" can serve as a bridge to promote global cooperation while avoiding a certain culture dominating AI development. 

Scenario 2 sounds ideal, but global consensus is difficult to achieve, and a single framework may ignore the uniqueness of certain cultures. Although it provides equal access opportunities, if a certain moral view becomes dominant, it may lead to technological monopoly and weaken diversity. 

Real-world cooperation is already challenging, and perhaps a more flexible AI system that respects differences is more suitable for future development.

场景 2听起来理想，但全球共识很难真正实现，单一框架可能会忽视某些文化的独特性。虽然它提供了平等访问的机会，但如果某种道德观成为主导，可能会导致技术垄断，削弱多元性。  

现实世界的合作本就充满挑战，或许一个更加灵活、尊重差异的 AI 体系才更适合未来发展。
